We are given a sequence of **1003 consecutive integers**, and the **sum of any three adjacent numbers is divisible by either 11 or 23**. We are to find the **largest possible last term** in this sequence.

### Step 1: Let the sequence be $ a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{1003} $

That is:
$$
a_i + a_{i+1} + a_{i+2} \equiv 0 \pmod{11} \quad \text{or} \quad a_i + a_{i+1} + a_{i+2} \equiv 0 \pmod{23}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
This must be divisible by **either 11 or 23**.

$$
3(a + i + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{11} \quad \text{or} \quad 3(a + i + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{23}
$$

$$

$$

$$

So, for each $ i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, 1001\} $, $ a + i + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{11} $ or $ a + i + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{23} $.
